security.label: Admin / internal
security.advice: Protect with authentication and send an X-Robots-Tag: noindex header. Listing it here only advertises where the login is.

security.label: Staging / dev
security.advice: Take staging and test environments off the public internet, or restrict them by IP or login. Use a noindex header rather than robots.txt.

security.label: Backups & archives
security.advice: Backups and archives should not be reachable over HTTP at all. Move them outside the web root and verify the URL returns 404.

security.label: Secrets & config
security.advice: Configuration files, version-control folders and credentials must never be web-accessible. Block them at the server and check they return 403 or 404.

security.label: Private APIs & debug
security.advice: Internal APIs and debug endpoints need authentication or a network allowlist. Crawlers are not the threat here; scripted scanners are.

security.label: User data & uploads
security.advice: Turn off directory listing and make sure private files require a login. A Disallow only asks polite crawlers to look away.

security.label: Version disclosure
security.advice: These files name the software and its version, which is what an attacker looks up first. Delete them from the server instead of hiding them here.

security.label: Maintenance scripts
security.advice: Installers and update scripts must not be reachable after setup. Remove them, or restrict them by IP address.

security.label: Server internals
security.advice: These paths belong to the server, not the site. If nothing runs there, remove the rule; it only points at them.
